scope: Frozen native decoder canaries: synthetic eSpeak positive speech and private emulator-noise controls with predetermined same-language trusted context. Not human-speech quality, held-out evaluation or production adoption.

source_binding.note: The informational source_checkout_commit does not identify these patched binaries; these explicit patch/source/library digests do.

baseline.source_checkout_note: Informational checkout only; binary/library hashes identify the measured engine, not proof it was built from this checkout.

candidate.source_checkout_note: Informational checkout only; binary/library hashes identify the measured engine, not proof it was built from this checkout.

policy.context: Empty for positive controls; predetermined same-language synthetic meeting phrase for noise. No Kotlin replay.

limitations: Synthetic eSpeak does not prove real human speech quality.
Positive controls use empty context; noise uses the same predetermined meeting-negation phrase for baseline and candidate in each language.
14noise cases cover only one trusted phrase per language, not every possible context.
One normal Spanish meeting sample reaches full-scale; synthesis validation documents this, input remains unchanged.
Short positive audio0.285–0.455s uses native1s padding, original-length filtering is retained.
No held-out access, downloads, production edits or phone speed claim.
public_export_note: Per-case profiles retain only timings, peak memory, original/padded frame counts and prompt identity. Common decoding settings are recorded once in policy; no native text diagnostics are exported.
